sections.overview: Micropterix aureatella is a very small, day-flying moth in the ancient family Micropterigidae.
sections.identification: Its wingspan is about 9–11 mm; the bronze-purple forewings bear broad golden bands and a median spot.
sections.habitat: In Britain it occurs in woodland and heathland, and is widespread though unevenly distributed; the species has a much broader Palearctic range.
sections.diet: Adults feed on pollen, particularly from sedges (Carex); the larval food is less certain, with a larva found in leaf litter among fungal hyphae.
sections.behavior: Adults fly by day in sunshine, and unlike most moths they retain working mandibles.
sections.reproduction: Adults are recorded from May to July in parts of Britain; the larval stage is present in early spring.
sections.ecology: It belongs to Micropterigidae, a lineage of moths with chewing adults; the family context helps distinguish it from later moth groups.
sections.conservation: No global conservation assessment was located; the regional British records cited here do not establish a global trend.
